**Author:** Daria Lepikhina, Independent Researcher  
**Original review date:** 18 October 2026  
**Published:** 19 October 2026, following the author's approval

**Canonical XB-1 source:** [holland202/sovereign-veritas](https://github.com/holland202/sovereign-veritas)  
**Review type:** source-only independent conceptual analysis, not experimental reproduction  

## Repository context

This is an independent conceptual review of the original public Sovereign Veritas XB-1/X5 source materials, not a reproduction or evaluation of later architectures.

## Short description

Independent conceptual review by **Daria Lepikhina, Independent Researcher**, of the published Sovereign Veritas XB-1 execution-boundary experiment, focusing on case X5 (a simulated external effect completed without a corresponding ledger record). The review considers what a human investigator could learn, who could intervene, how record correction differs from remedying consequences, and which human-oversight questions could be tested in a follow-up scenario.

**Scope and limitations:** The author reviewed the published results, preregistration, and probe code. This is a **source-only conceptual review**, not an independent execution or reproduction of XB-1, an audit of other Sovereign Veritas components, validation of the wider system, or evidence of actual harm. Proposed safeguards and human-response scenarios are future research questions, not established system capabilities or experimental findings.

**Attribution and independence:** This document reflects the author's own analysis and is not an endorsement of Sovereign Veritas or its conclusions. The author approved the review and accompanying description for publication before release. No implied transfer of ownership or additional co-authorship.
